newsitem.title: GREECE: RALLYING-FORD LEAD THE WAY IN ACROPOLIS RALLY.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-FORD LEAD THE WAY IN ACROPOLIS RALLY.

text.p: The Ford duo of Finn Juha Kankkunen and Spain's Carlos Sainz pulled clear in the Acropolis Rally on Monday.

Kankkunen, who had started the day with a 27-second lead over the Mitsubishis of Briton Richard Burns and Finland's Tommi Makinen, had seen his advantage over Burns cut to 17 seconds at the end of the 10th stage, but slowly rebuilt it to 37 seconds over Sainz as the teams stopped overnight in Kamena Vourla.
Burns was unable to match the Fords and, after a spin on the 12th stage which cost him almost 20 seconds, was overtaken by Sainz on the final stage of the day, the 14th of the rally.
Double champion Sainz was in unstoppable form and set the fastest time in six of the day's seven stages as the Ford team look set to secure their first victory of the season.
"Sainz has just been driving well all day and these are just the kind of conditions he loves," said a Ford team member. "To be fastest on six of the day's stages is a fantastic achievement."
A victory for Sainz on Tuesday would put him back into contention for the world championship, although Kankkunen will be keen to secure his first win since the Rally of Portugal in 1994.

With Burns finishing the 14th stage in third position, world championship leader Makinen was fourth more than four minutes behind Kankkunen after suffering a broken rear suspension and a broken driveshaft on the punishing mountain roads.

The conditions, which had already claimed championship challenger Briton Colin McRae in the Subaru on Monday, took care of his team-mate on Tuesday when Swede Kenneth Eriksson dropped out with steering failure after landing heavily from a jump.

"Everything was going fine and I had no concerns," explained Eriksson, who had been running in 14th position after a roll on the opening day. "We were going through a fast left-hander and then onto a straight over a jump.

"When we landed I felt something was wrong with the steering so we stopped and checked and saw that the track rod end had bent. We managed to fix it so we could continue, but eventually the strain on it was too much and it broke."

That eighth stage was later cancelled when the Ford of Monaco's Jean-Pierre Richelmi rolled out of the event and burst into flames. Although the crew were unhurt, officials had to suspend the stage so the car could be cleared.
The incident led to confusion on the next stage at Makrirahi when spectators accidently blocked the drivers after a large gap between the 15th and 16th cars saw them wander onto the road.
The final leg of the rally on Tuesday afternoon will take the teams to Athens.
